verdict.rationale: Honeycomb's native alerting is threshold-based: triggers fire on "thresholds that you define" [honeycomb-docs-6], and SLO alerts fire on budget burn, which still depends on a defined objective [honeycomb-docs-7]. The only outlier evidence is that AI agents connected through the MCP server can "identify performance outliers" [honeycomb-docs-10], [honeycomb-docs-20], which needs an external agent rather than an enable-able alerting feature. BubbleUp appears on the pricing page [honeycomb-docs-53] but is never described, so it can't be credited as anomaly detection. Missing for 10: a native, enable-able anomaly or outlier detection feature, threshold-free alerting on detected anomalies, documentation of what BubbleUp does, and independent or hands-on corroboration.
